record.paper_title: Some open problems on Feynman periods
record.original_question: Is every period of every Feynman graph with at most 5 loops a multiple zeta value? Equivalently, do the graphs with loop number ≤ 5 avoid genuinely non-MZV periods even in the cases where current methods only show that their periods are rational linear combinations of alternating sums or multiple polylogarithms at −1?

evidence.quote: The interesting observation is that all graphs with ≤ 5 loops seem to have only MZV as periods [1, 34, 35]; that is, all periods of the supposedly more complicated graphs (the non-planar ones and the cube) turn out to be MZV.
Conjecture 3. All periods of graphs with ≤ 5 loops are multiple zeta values.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Consider scalar massless φ⁴ theory in four dimensions. To each connected 4-regular graph G obtained as a Feynman graph in this theory (equivalently, after taking a vertex at infinity, a 4-regular graph with one vertex removed) one associates its period P(G), defined as the convergent projective integral
   P(G) = ∫_{x_i ≥ 0} (1/Ψ_G(x)^2) Ω,
where Ψ_G is the (first) Symanzik/Kirchhoff polynomial of G and Ω = Σ_i (−1)^i x_i dx_1 ∧ … ∧ d̂x_i ∧ … ∧ dx_n is the standard projective volume form on the simplex {x_i ≥ 0}/ℝ_{>0}. The "loop number" (first Betti number) of G is denoted ℓ(G).

A multiple zeta value (MZV) is a real number of the form
   ζ(s_1, s_2, …, s_k) = Σ_{n_1 > n_2 > … > n_k ≥ 1} 1/(n_1^{s_1} n_2^{s_2} ⋯ n_k^{s_k}),
where s_i are positive integers and s_1 ≥ 2. Let MZV ⊂ ℝ denote the ℚ-vector space spanned by all multiple zeta values. (Equivalently, MZV is the ℚ-span of iterated integrals of dt/t and dt/(1−t) from 0 to 1.)

Question. Is it true that for every connected Feynman graph G arising in massless φ⁴ theory with loop number ℓ(G) ≤ 5, the period P(G) lies in MZV?

(In particular, for those graphs at ℓ(G) ≤ 5 whose periods are presently known only to be ℚ-linear combinations of alternating Euler sums or values of multiple polylogarithms at −1, do these combinations always reduce to multiple zeta values?)
artifact.category_tag: Feynman periods and multiple zeta values
artifact.status_search_result: Computational evidence (Broadhurst–Kreimer, Schnetz, and follow-up work) shows that all known periods of φ⁴ graphs up to 6 (and partly up to 7) loops evaluate to multiple zeta values, with new non-MZV periods first appearing at 7–8 loops. However, no published proof asserts that every ≤5-loop period must lie in MZV; the statement remains a conjecture supported by numerical evaluations rather than a theorem.

status_evidence.title: Predicting Feynman periods in φ⁴ theory
status_evidence.snippet: Up to six loops all periods are known to be multiple zeta values; new types of periods (non-MZV) appear at higher loop orders.
status_evidence.claim: Computations confirm MZV-only periods through 6 loops, supporting (but not proving) the ≤5-loop conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Field Theory over F_q (Schnetz)
status_evidence.snippet: Residues in φ⁴ theory have been computed up to six loops and for some graphs up to nine loops; non-MZV periods appear beyond low loop orders.
status_evidence.claim: No counterexample at ≤5 loops; status of the conjecture remains an empirical observation.
